item.title: On a generalization of result due to Peskine and Szpiro-II
item.description: arXiv:2611.18500v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $(R,\mathfrak{m})$ be a regular local ring and let $I$ be a Cohen-Macaulay ideal of $R$. When $\operatorname{Char} R=p>0$, a result of Peskine and Szpiro proves that $H^i_I(R)=0$ for $i\neq\operatorname{height} I$. This result is not true when $\operatorname{Char} R=0$. In this article, we prove that the Bass numbers of $H^{\operatorname{height} I}_I(R)$ completely determines the vanishing of $H^i_I(R)$ for $i\neq \operatorname{height} I$. This result was previously established by the second author in the equicharacteristic case and more generally for Gorenstein local rings by Hellus and Schenzel. In contrast to the spectral sequence methods employed by Hellus and Schenzel, our proof is elementary and self-contained.
item.dc:creator: Sayed Sadiqul Islam, Tony J. Puthenpurakal

item.title: Inequalities for intersection numbers from Hodge-Riemann relations
item.description: arXiv:2611.17841v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We derived inequalities for intersection numbers of nef classes inside algebras satisfying the K\"ahler package, using Hodge-Riemann relations up to degree two. As an application, we construct certain strictly Lorentzian polynomials and show that they cannot be realized as the volume polynomial of nef classes inside such an algebra.
item.dc:creator: Xiangru Zeng

item.title: A Helly theorem for the Bruhat-Tits building
item.description: arXiv:2611.17844v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $K$ be a discretely valued field with valuation ring $\mathcal{O}$. We show that a finite family of $\mathcal{O}$-lattices in $K^m$ is adapted to a common basis if any subfamily of at most $m+1$ $\mathcal{O}$-lattices is. In other words, in the Bruhat-Tits building of $\operatorname{GL}(m)$, a finite family of simplices lies in a common apartment if and only if any subfamily of at most $m+1$ simplices does. The proof uses a version of Radon's theorem for $\mathcal{O}$-lattices. We also give an alternative proof using truncated modules.
item.dc:creator: Rudrendra Kashyap, Kiumars Kaveh, Christopher Manon, Boris Tsvelikhovskiy

item.title: The $\operatorname{Proj}$ construction for pro-graded Huber pairs
item.description: arXiv:2611.18374v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Inspired by the theory of pro-graded adic rings developed recently by Ishizuka and Yoshikawa, we introduce and study the notions of a pro-graded Huber ring and a pro-graded Huber pair \begin{equation*}((\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{A}_{\textrm{gr}}), \mathcal{A}^{+}),\end{equation*}which capture the intuition of a complete Huber ring (or Huber pair) equipped with a dense graded subring. Using these notions, we define and study an analog \begin{equation*}\operatorname{Proj}(\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{A}_{\textrm{gr}}, \mathcal{A}^{+})\end{equation*}of the $\operatorname{Proj}$ construction from algebraic geometry in the realm of adic spaces, without restricting our attention to adic spaces satisfying any Noetherian or finite-type assumptions. We consider gradings both by $\mathbb{Z}$ and by $\mathbb{Z}[1/p]$ for a fixed prime number $p$, so our $\operatorname{Proj}$ construction recovers both classical examples such as usual adic projective space $\mathbb{P}_{K}^{n,\textrm{ad}}$ and infinite-type, perfectoid examples such as perfectoid projective space $\mathbb{P}_{K}^{n,\textrm{perfd}}$. Using GAGA, we prove that the adic analytification of any projective variety $X$ over a nonarchimedean field $K$ can be described as the adic $\operatorname{Proj}$ of a suitable pro-graded affinoid algebra $\mathcal{A}$. Moreover, we prove that in this case $\dim X=\dim \mathcal{A}-1$. We also relate our adic $\operatorname{Proj}$ construction to formal models.
item.dc:creator: Dimitri Dine

item.title: A quotient formula for the Behrend function
item.description: arXiv:2611.18432v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Behrend function is essential in enumerative geometry. However, computing it, even in zero dimension, has been a highly subtle and mysterious matter since its introduction in the 2000s. We present a quotient formula for the Behrend function of any closed $r$-dimensional affine scheme $X^r \subset \mathbb{A}^N$, evaluated at a singular point, where $0\leq r \leq N-1$. In particular, if the scheme is monomial, we associate parallelepipeds to it and interpret the Behrend function as simple volume information about them. The results here, in particular, recover the recent results of Graffeo-Ricolfi for the zero-dimensional case in 2D in \cite{Graffeo-Ricolfi}, and also the more recent result of Polini-Sammartan-Ulrich on the zero-dimensional case in \cite{PSU26}.
item.dc:creator: Fatemeh Rezaee

item.title: Minimal Systems of Binomial Generators for the Ideals of Certain Monomial Curves
item.description: arXiv:2111.03714v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $a, b$ and $n > 1$ be three positive integers such that $a$ and $\sum_{j=0}^{n-1} b^j$ are relatively prime. In this paper, we prove that the toric ideal $I$ associated to the submonoid of $\mathbb{N}$ generated by $\{\sum_{j=0}^{n-1} b^j\} \cup \{\sum_{j=0}^{n-1} b^j + a\, \sum_{j=0}^{i-2} b^j \mid i = 2, \ldots, n\}$ is determinantal. Moreover, we prove that for $n > 3$, the ideal $I$ has a unique minimal system of generators if and only if $a < b-1$.
item.dc:creator: Manuel B. Branco, Isabel Cola\c{c}o, Ignacio Ojeda

item.title: The Column-Diamond Resolution over Quadratic Monomial Rings
item.description: arXiv:2408.14695v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study infinite minimal free resolutions of modules $M = R/(x_{i_1},\ldots,x_{i_m})$ over quadratic monomial rings $R = k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/I$. We introduce the Column-Diamond construction, a recursive diagrammatic procedure that builds an explicit free resolution of $M$ from columns and diamonds determined by the quadratic generators of $I$. We prove that this resolution is exact and minimal. As an application, the Betti numbers of $M$ are counted by valid words in a graph associated to $I$, which yields a combinatorial rational formula for the Poincar\'e series.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Bravo, Federico Castillo, Nelly Villamizar

item.title: Ideals generated by corner-interval minors
item.description: arXiv:2506.09618v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article, we study binomial ideals generated by an arbitrary collection of corner-interval $2$-minors of a generic matrix. We determine the minimal prime ideals of such ideals and characterize their radicality in the special case of corner minors. Moreover, we discuss connectivity properties of contingency tables in algebraic statistics. We compute the Hilbert-Poincar\'e polynomial of the ideal generated by the set of all corner-interval minors and we derive the formula for the regularity in the case of corner minors.
item.dc:creator: Marie Amalore Nambi
